open-question.question: Does `capture-milestone-principle-updates` keep its required positional milestone argument, now a path, or take the same required `--milestone <path>` as every other per-milestone skill, given that today it is the stated exception because the milestone it harvests is named rather than current, and that under the new shape every milestone is named?
open-question.recommendation: Capture harvests any milestone, finished and removed ones included, which the shared resolution does not accept, so a bare positional path keeps that difference visible instead of hiding two validations behind one flag, and it is the smallest change.
open-question.alternative: Capture keeps a required positional argument, now the milestone's repo-relative path as the definition tool printed it, used verbatim in the repeat-capture grep, the path-scoped answer walk, and the `Principle-capture:` subject. It parses no `--milestone`, does not resolve through `get-current-milestone.md`, and keeps its own existence test and its own two fixed stop lines (reworded from "id" to "path"). It stays the stated exception in the resolution invariant, its reason restated: the milestone it harvests may already be finished and removed, which the shared resolution does not accept. The smallest change. Capture's own test can accept a removed directory without touching the resolution that every other skill shares, and the procedure stays a live-milestone resolution only. One value now has two argument shapes. The old reason for the exception (named rather than current) no longer holds, because every milestone is now named, so a chain or harness has to remember that this one skill takes the path bare while the other seventeen-odd take `--milestone`. The invariant has to keep a carve-out that is justified only by removal.

Capture takes the same required `--milestone <path>` as every other per-milestone skill. It recognises the flag by the procedure's rule and resolves through `get-current-milestone.md`, so its two own stop lines give way to the procedure's shared stops. Its exception clause is removed from the resolution invariant, and the resolved path feeds the grep, the walk, and the subject verbatim. One argument shape, one resolution seam, and one set of stop lines across the plugin. Capture's carve-out and its separately worded checks leave the invariant and the fixed-lines table, and every chain writes capture's line the same way as its neighbours. The shared procedure matches only when `<path>/requirements.md` exists, so capturing a milestone right after finish removes its directory works only if the shared resolution itself learns to accept a removed path. Every other skill would then inherit that acceptance, or the procedure would need a mode for it. This depends on how the sibling "Removed milestone addressing" and "Resolution match test" questions settle.

Capture takes the same required `--milestone <path>` flag, written and recognised by the procedure's one rule, so its usage line matches the other skills'. It validates the value itself instead of resolving through `get-current-milestone.md`: its own existence test, which may accept a removed directory, and its own fixed stop lines. The invariant names it as the one skill that takes the shared flag but checks it separately. Callers see one uniform flag on every per-milestone line, while the shared resolution stays strict about live milestones. Accepting a finished, removed milestone stays local to the one skill that needs it. One flag gets two validation homes and two meanings: "a live milestone" everywhere else, "any milestone, history included" here. That is a split the surface hides and that a reader of a failed call cannot see. Capture also keeps stop lines worded differently from the procedure's for what looks like the same mistake. How far its test departs from the shared one depends on the sibling "Removed milestone addressing" question.

open-question.question: Does this milestone rewrite the maintainer-only `/release-plugin` skill, whose steps 3c and 7 gather release notes from `Milestone-finish:` commits path-scoped to `milestones/README.md` and from its `### Milestone` headings, to read the finish commit bodies instead, or is that left to the release that ships the change, given that the Goal cuts no release inside the milestone and that the next release's notes would otherwise find nothing?
open-question.recommendation: The breaking release is the first whose notes the old reader cannot gather, so its reader should exist before it is needed, and reading the finished milestones and their summaries through the tool parses the body contract and the trailer rule in one place rather than a second time in plain git.
open-question.alternative: This milestone carries a task that rewrites step 5a–5e of `/release-plugin` to read the record through the milestones tool's history queries, not through a `git log` of its own. `milestones .` supplies the finished milestones with their finish dates, the skill keeps those finished after the last tag's date, and `summary` on each one supplies its title line and bullets for that milestone's `###` section. The README cross-check is dropped, and steps 3c and 7, which read `CHANGELOG.md`, stay as they are. Release notes read the finish records through the same tested parser as every runtime reader (`discuss-milestone-goal`, `ask-in-milestone-context`). The body contract and any trailer rule are then parsed in one place only, so a later change to the finish body cannot quietly break the release notes. A maintainer-only skill outside `core/` comes to depend on a tool's command path and on line shapes this milestone is still settling (the Milestones query line, Live summary print, and Trailer in finish body axes), so the rewrite can only be written once those land. It still depends on migrated commits carrying the original finish dates (the Migration commit mechanism axis), and it adds a task to a milestone of about fourteen tasks whose Goal does not name the release skill.

This milestone carries a task that rewrites the note gathering in `/release-plugin`. That gathering is step 5a–5e: 5a takes the commit side from `Milestone-finish:` subjects path-scoped to `milestones/README.md`, 5b takes the history side from a diff of the README's `### Milestone` headings, 5c cross-checks the two, and 5e reads each README entry. Steps 3c and 7 read only `CHANGELOG.md` and stay as they are. The new gathering reads the finish commits directly with the skill's own `git log`: it takes every `Milestone-finish: ` subject with its body, keeps a milestone when the commit's author date is later than the last tag's, and builds each `###` section from the body's title line and bullets. The README cross-check is dropped, because the finish commit becomes the only record and there is no second side to compare. The skill's other README mentions, such as the zsh example `$LAST_TAG:milestones/README.md`, are reworded in the same task. The milestones tool is not used. The breaking release is the first one whose notes the old reader cannot gather, and with this option its reader exists and is tested before it is needed: in the range 1.9.0..HEAD it collects milestones 51–53 through their migrated bodies and 54 through its native body. The skill also stays as self-contained as it is today, using plain git commands like every other step and calling no plugin tool. The selection depends on migrated finish commits carrying the original finish author dates. The commit range alone would also pick up the migration's commits for milestones 1–50, which earlier releases already covered. So this option depends on how the migration sets its dates (the Migration commit mechanism and Migration missing finish date axes). It also parses the body contract a second time, outside the tool, including how a trailing attribution block is handled (the Trailer in finish body axis). And it adds a task to a milestone sized at about fourteen tasks, whose Goal names commit subjects, chains, host trees, docs, and `CLAUDE.md` but not the release skill.

This milestone rewrites `/release-plugin` so that finish records stop feeding the release notes. The skill's empty-range path (step 5d, which condenses the range's commit subjects, and their bodies where a subject is unclear, into bulleted notes) becomes the only way notes are composed. Steps 5a–5c and 5e, along with every README read, are removed, and steps 3c and 7 stay as they are. Neither the README nor the finish commit bodies are read for notes. The release notes no longer depend on the finish body contract, on migrated author dates, or on any milestones-tool query shape. The rewrite can therefore be written now, independent of every sibling still open, and it cannot break when the record's shape changes again. The notes lose the per-milestone `### <Title> (milestone N)` sections that every release since 0.9.8 has carried. Each release instead has to condense hundreds of commits, most of them annotation and answer commits, which repeats work the finish summaries already did. This option also ignores the finish summary written for the record, the only text in the record written for exactly this purpose.

This milestone leaves `.claude/skills/release-plugin/SKILL.md` unchanged and gives it no task. The note gathering is rewritten later, outside this milestone, before the next release is cut: either in a maintainer commit made when that release is prepared, or in a later milestone ahead of it. That rewrite also decides the reader's source and selection rule. Until it lands, `/release-plugin` stops at its step 5c cross-check, with nothing changed and nothing published. Once the migration removes `milestones/README.md`, the history side reads no headings, while the commit side still finds milestones 51–53's old finish commits in the range. The milestone keeps exactly the scope its Goal states and cuts no release. The skill is rendered into no host tree and reaches no user project, so nothing a user runs depends on it in the meantime. The rewrite can also be written against the queries and finish bodies as they actually landed, and tried on the real range when the release is cut. The breaking release is the one whose notes have to name the upgrade step, and with this option it is the first run of a reader nobody has written or tried. Meanwhile the tree carries a maintainer skill that is known to stop at its own cross-check. The design draft also lists "the release notes follow" among this milestone's pieces, so deferring leaves that piece undone with no recorded owner.
